article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 55% Sativa / 45% Indica
Genetics: Blueberry × OG Kush
Breeder: Dinafem Seeds
THC Content: 20%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Lemon, pine, red berries, sweet fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 60 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: 500 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 600–800 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

Blue Kush brings together two cannabis families that became famous for almost opposite reasons. Blueberry earned its reputation through sweet fruit, colorful flowers, and a smooth character, while OG Kush built its identity around resin, pine, citrus, earth, and a far more penetrating potency. Dinafem combined the two to create a plant that does not simply taste like berry-flavored Kush. The cultivar can move from fresh lemon and pine into red fruit and resin, with the sweeter Blueberry influence softening the sharper OG foundation without hiding it. Under cooler nighttime temperatures, the plants may develop purple, violet, and lavender coloration that makes the Blue ancestry visible before the flower is even sampled.

Its effects follow the same theme of balance. Blue Kush carries a slight sativa majority at roughly 55%, but the experience combines long-lasting cerebral stimulation with a physical relaxation substantial enough to make the strain feel considerably heavier than that percentage suggests. A 60-day flowering period, vigorous growth, strong moisture resistance, and breeder-listed yields of around 500 g/m² indoors make it practical as well as attractive. Dinafem designed the cultivar to be approachable even for inexperienced growers, creating a weed strain where visual appeal and sophisticated flavor do not require an unusually demanding cultivation routine.
Genetics and Lineage

Dinafem created Blue Kush from Blueberry × OG Kush. The Blueberry parent used in the project was an original selection maintained by the breeder and chosen around the year 2000. Blueberry itself is one of the defining achievements of breeder DJ Short and traces to a blend of Afghan indica and tropical sativa ancestry, including Thai-related genetics. Generations of selection produced the sweet berry fragrance, colorful pigmentation, resin production, and distinctive hybrid effects for which the Blue family became famous.

OG Kush contributes a very different set of characteristics. Although the deeper historical origins of OG Kush remain disputed, the cultivar’s breeding influence is well established. Dense resin, strong potency, citrus and pine aromas, earthy depth, and a sturdy Kush-like character became hallmarks of the line. Dinafem used the OG parent to reinforce structure and intensity while allowing Blueberry to contribute sweetness and visual color. The resulting offspring retain enough vertical vigor to be classified slightly toward the sativa side while developing dense buds more commonly associated with indica-influenced marijuana.

The parents complement one another particularly well in their aromatic profiles. Blueberry supplies red-fruit and berry sweetness, whereas OG Kush contributes fresh citrus, evergreen, earth, and resin. Neither side disappears inside the cross. That balance is also visible in plant morphology: leaves remain relatively small, internodal spacing is moderate, and flower sites distribute themselves evenly across sturdy branches. This makes Blue Kush more than a combination of two famous names; its defining traits can be traced clearly back to both parental families.
Effects and Experience

The experience often begins mentally rather than physically. A noticeable cerebral lift can make thoughts feel lighter and surroundings more engaging, while conversation, music, or quiet creative activity may become more absorbing. Dinafem describes the mental stimulation as gentle but long lasting, which separates the cultivar from intensely racy sativas that peak rapidly and can become mentally exhausting. The effect has energy, but that energy is cushioned by the Kush side of the pedigree.

Physical relaxation develops alongside the cerebral component rather than replacing it completely. The body begins to feel more comfortable, muscular tension fades, and the overall pace of the experience slows. At moderate doses this creates a particularly balanced state in which the consumer can feel mentally engaged and physically at ease at the same time. Larger servings can shift the balance further toward heaviness and may eventually produce pronounced lethargy or sleepiness.

Dinafem places THC around 20%, with very low CBD, giving Blue Kush meaningful potency without relying on the extreme laboratory numbers associated with some modern cultivars. That strength can still be substantial for occasional consumers. Dry mouth and dry eyes are common possibilities, while an unnecessarily large dose may lead to dizziness, temporary anxiety, or mental fog. Smaller amounts better preserve the strain’s distinctive combination of cerebral stimulation and body-centered relaxation.
Medical Benefits

The balanced nature of the effects may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who want relief without immediately becoming sedated. During the earlier stage, the clearer mental lift may make everyday stress, low mood, or emotional fatigue feel less dominant. Because the physical component develops at the same time, muscular tightness and general discomfort may also become easier to ignore without completely removing motivation.

As the dose increases, relaxation becomes deeper and the cultivar can shift toward evening use. Appetite may become stronger, the body can feel progressively heavier, and rest becomes more appealing. This dose-dependent change gives Blue Kush more flexibility than marijuana that remains strictly stimulating or heavily sedating throughout the entire session. Consumers with lower THC tolerance should nevertheless approach it conservatively because a roughly 20% THC cultivar can still create pronounced impairment.

Dinafem does not publish one standardized terpene laboratory panel for Blue Kush. The documented aroma of citrus, pine, berries, and Kush resin indicates a complex volatile profile, but exact terpene ratios will vary according to phenotype and cultivation environment. Medical users should rely on testing from the actual batch when available and consider personal cannabinoid sensitivity, medications, and previous responses to cannabis rather than assuming the strain name guarantees a particular therapeutic outcome.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fresh citrus and pine form the sharpest part of the bouquet. Lemon-like brightness appears quickly when mature buds are opened, while evergreen resin provides a dry, slightly woody edge beneath it. These characteristics come through strongly from the OG Kush side and keep the aroma crisp rather than overly sweet. There is also an earthy foundation that becomes more noticeable once the flower is broken apart.

Blueberry influence arrives as the softer counterpoint. Red berries and sweet fruit round out the sharper lemon-and-pine combination, creating a flavor that feels more refined than straightforward Kush. Some plants may emphasize fruit more strongly, while others remain dominated by citrus and resin. Cooler temperatures can deepen flower color dramatically, but purple pigmentation does not necessarily predict which aromatic direction a particular phenotype will favor.

On the palate, citrus and pine generally appear first before sweet berry notes become clearer through the middle of the inhale. Earthy Kush lingers after exhalation and gives the flavor enough weight to remain persistent. Vaporization can preserve more of the fruit and fresh citrus character, while combustion tends to emphasize pine, earth, and resin. A careful cure helps keep the lighter berry notes intact rather than allowing the stronger Kush foundation to dominate the finished flower.
Growing Information

Blue Kush is unusually forgiving for a cultivar combining two elite genetic families. Dinafem describes the plants as hardy, vigorous, resistant to moisture, and adaptable to a wide range of indoor techniques. They develop a sturdy medium-sized frame with relatively small leaves, moderate internodal distance, and evenly distributed flowering sites. SOG , SCROG , hydroponic systems , or conventional soil cultivation can all work effectively, which makes the strain suitable for growers who prefer very different garden styles.

Indoor flowering takes about 60 days, with yields of approximately 500 g/m² under good conditions. The flowers become long, dense, and highly resinous as maturity approaches. Nighttime temperature drops of around 10°C can intensify anthocyanin expression, producing lavender, violet, and purple hues associated with Blueberry ancestry. Color should be treated as a genetic trait rather than the main cultivation objective, however; stable irrigation, sufficient light, airflow, and balanced nutrition remain more important for final flower quality.

Outdoors, the breeder lists production around 600–800 grams per plant, with maturity arriving from early to mid-October. Plants reach roughly 1.5 meters under typical conditions and perform best in warm, dry, temperate climates or protected greenhouse environments. Their moisture resistance gives them an advantage over more delicate dense-bud cultivars, although prolonged autumn rain can still create problems. Blue Kush is also not especially demanding nutritionally, making a standard feeding program more appropriate than aggressive fertilization.
FAQ
What strains make Blue Kush?

Blue Kush was bred by Dinafem Seeds from Blueberry × OG Kush. Blueberry contributes berry sweetness, colorful pigmentation, and hybrid vigor, while OG Kush adds citrus, pine, earth, resin, and stronger physical effects.
Is Blue Kush indica or sativa?
Dinafem classifies Blue Kush as approximately 55% sativa and 45% indica. Its effects are notably balanced, combining long-lasting cerebral stimulation with substantial physical relaxation.
How much THC does Blue Kush have?

Dinafem lists Blue Kush at approximately 20% THC with low CBD. Breeder data places CBD around 0.16%, although cannabinoid concentrations can vary according to phenotype, environment, cultivation method, and harvest maturity.
What does Blue Kush taste like?

The primary flavor combines fresh citrus, pine, red berries, sweet fruit, and earthy Kush. OG Kush provides the sharper lemon-and-evergreen side, while Blueberry contributes the softer fruit character.
How long does Blue Kush take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately 60 days. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity from early to mid-October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Final Thoughts on Blue Kush

Blue Kush works because its two parents retain recognizable roles inside the finished cultivar. Blueberry contributes sweetness, berry fruit, and the possibility of striking violet coloration, while OG Kush supplies citrus, pine, earth, resin, and a stronger physical backbone. Instead of one parent overwhelming the other, the cross creates a genuinely balanced expression of both genetic families.

The cultivation characteristics make that quality unusually accessible. A roughly 60-day flowering period, indoor production near 500 g/m², outdoor yields of approximately 600–800 grams per plant, moisture resistance, and compatibility with SOG, SCROG, hydroponics, or conventional gardens give growers considerable flexibility. Its relatively forgiving nature also makes Blue Kush a practical introduction to more sophisticated genetics for less experienced cultivators.

For consumers, the strain offers more than colorful flowers. Lemon and pine bring brightness, berries supply sweetness, and earthy Kush provides depth, while the high moves between cerebral stimulation and lasting physical calm. Blue Kush remains one of Dinafem’s more complete hybrids because appearance, flavor, garden performance, and effects all express the same central idea: bringing the contrasting personalities of Blueberry and OG Kush together without sacrificing what made either parent distinctive.
